- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if sentiment turns negative, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect early reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth 3–5 day moving average of history before forecasting to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 7-day window as anchor for forecast stability.
